To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neutropenia in the G6PC3 mouse is caused by a combination of survival and functional deficiencies in neutrophil differentiation.
G6PC3-deficient neutrophil granule precursors show a reduced survival and a reduced capacity for glucose utilization, which results in a reduced differentiation into functional neutrophils.

G6PC3-deficient neutrophils show a combination of survival and differentiation defects, both originating from reduced glucose utilization, that can be rescued in part by transgenic expression of BCL-XL, but cannot be fully rescued in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of glucose-6-phosphate in neutrophil differentiation and survival, which may be relevant for the treatment of neutropenic diseases.
the role of glucose metabolism in the development of neutrophils and the consequences of a defect in glucose utilization in the generation of mature neutrophils.
the differentiation of the neutrophils from the bone marrow and their survival in the periphery, which is important for immune responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
G6PC3 is essential for the survival of myeloid progenitors and for neutrophil differentiation, and that it is required for normal glucose utilization in these processes.
G6PC3 is required in neutrophils for their normal survival, differentiation and maturation.

G6PC3-deficient cells show a profound differentiation and functional defect that is linked to a reduced ability to metabolize glucose and that is associated with ER stress, apoptosis, reduced proliferation and reduced cytokine production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
G6PC3-deficient neutrophils are functionally deficient due to impaired glucose utilization and ER stress, which causes apoptosis and a loss of neutrophil elastases.
the G6PC3 protein is a key regulator of glucose metabolism and that its deficiency causes neutropenias by interfering with both differentiation and survival of neutrophil cells.

the G6PC3-deficient cells show defects in differentiation and apoptosis, and that the apoptosis defect can be rescued by Bcl-xL, however, at the cost of differentiation and function of the mature cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
G6PC3-deficient neutrophil progenitor cells show reduced survival, which can be rescued by Bcl-XL.
G6PC3 is required for normal glucose metabolism in myeloid cells, with a profound effect on survival and differentiation.
G6PC3 is required to support neutrophil differentiation and survival.
